results.title: Correctness of the Shannon expansion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be a list of atoms and let $f$ assign a truth value to every valuation of the atoms, such that $f(v) = f(w)$ whenever $v$ and $w$ agree on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. results.title: Functional completeness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every Boolean function of the atoms in a finite list is the truth table, on valuations with `⊥` false, of some proposition.

results.title: Propositions built from $\to$ and $\bot$
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Translation into $\to$ and $\bot$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The translation $A^*$ of a proposition $A$ is defined by recursion on $A$: each atom is unchanged, $(A \to B)^* = A^* \to B^*$, $(A \wedge B)^* = (A^* \to (B^* \to \bot)) \to \bot$ and $(A \vee B)^* = (A^* \to \bot) \to B^*$.

results.title: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves truth values

results.title: Composition factor of a group (via subnormal subgroups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For groups $T$ and $Q$, $T$ is a composition factor of $Q$ when some subnormal subgroup $H$ of $Q$ maps onto $T$, that is, there is a surjective group homomorphism $H \to T$. Here $H$ is subnormal in $Q$ when there is a finite chain of subgroups $H = H_0 \le H_1 \le \dots \le H_k = Q$ in which each $H_j$ is normal in $H_{j+1}$.

results.title: Upper composition factors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For groups $T$ and $G$, $T$ is an upper composition factor of $G$ when it is a composition factor of some finite quotient of $G$: there are a finite group $Q$ and a surjective group homomorphism $G \to Q$ such that $T$ is a composition factor of $Q$, that is, $T$ is a homomorphic image of a subnormal subgroup of $Q$.

results.title: Segal's theorem on upper composition factors, 63 generators (Kourovka Problem 11.57)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every family $(T_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite non-abelian simple groups there is a group $G$ generated by $63$ elements such that a finite simple group $Q$ is an upper composition factor of $G$ (a composition factor of some finite quotient of $G$) if and only if $Q$ is isomorphic to $T_i$ for some $i \in I$. results.title: TRIP-Stern tree
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A TRIP-Stern tree with node values in a type $\alpha$ consists of a root seed in $\alpha$ together with two maps from $\alpha$ to $\alpha$, the left transition and the right transition. No condition is imposed on the seed or on the two transitions; in the source the seed is $(1,1,1)$ and the left and right transitions are induced by the maps $F_0$ and $F_1$ defined there.

results.title: Node selected by a binary path
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with seed $s$, left transition $L$ and right transition $R$. A binary path is a finite sequence of steps, each left or right. The node of $T$ selected by a path $(b_1, \dots, b_k)$ is obtained by starting at $s$ and applying, for $i = 1, \dots, k$ in order, $L$ if $b_i$ is a left step and $R$ if $b_i$ is a right step.

results.title: The empty path selects the seed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, the node of $T$ selected by the empty binary path is the seed of $T$.

results.title: Extending a path by a left step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with left transition $L$. For every binary path $p$, the node of $T$ selected by $p$ followed by one left step equals $L$ applied to the node of $T$ selected by $p$.

results.title: Extending a path by a right step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with right transition $R$. For every binary path $p$, the node of $T$ selected by $p$ followed by one right step equals $R$ applied to the node of $T$ selected by $p$.

results.title: Nodes at a given depth of a TRIP-Stern tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree and $n$ a natural number. The set of nodes of $T$ at depth $n$ is the set of all values $y$ such that some binary path of length $n$ selects $y$ in $T$.

results.title: Membership in a level of a TRIP-Stern tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, natural number $n$ and node value $y$, $y$ lies in the set of nodes of $T$ at depth $n$ if and only if there is a binary path of length $n$ whose selected node in $T$ is $y$.

results.title: Depth zero is the seed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$ and every node value $y$, $y$ lies in the set of nodes of $T$ at depth $0$ if and only if $y$ is the seed of $T$.

results.title: Left-most node of a TRIP-Stern tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with seed $s$ and left transition $L$. The left-most node of $T$ at depth $n$ is $L^n(s)$, the result of applying $L$ $n$ times to $s$; that is, it is $s$ at depth $0$, and at depth $n + 1$ it is $L$ applied to the left-most node at depth $n$.

results.title: Rightmost node of a TRIP-Stern tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a TRIP-Stern tree $T$ and a natural number $n$, the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $n$ is obtained from the seed of $T$ by applying the right transition of $T$ exactly $n$ times: at depth $0$ it is the seed, and at depth $n + 1$ it is the image of the rightmost node at depth $n$ under the right transition.

results.title: Left-most node at depth zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, the left-most node of $T$ at depth $0$ is the seed of $T$.

results.title: Recursion for the left-most node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with left transition $L$. For every natural number $n$, the left-most node of $T$ at depth $n + 1$ equals $L$ applied to the left-most node of $T$ at depth $n$.

results.title: Rightmost node at depth zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $0$ is the seed of $T$.

results.title: Successor step of the rightmost node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$ and every natural number $n$, the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $n + 1$ is the image of the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $n$ under the right transition of $T$.

results.title: Decoding a Turing machine head move
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Decode a head move: `0` moves left, `1` stays, anything else moves right.

results.title: Coded actions
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A coded action for a machine with $k$ work tapes consists of a coded input-head move; for each of the $k$ work tapes, an optional symbol to write, the symbol being a bit or the blank (so a blank can be written), together with a coded head move; an optional output bit; and an optional next state in $\mathbb{N}$, where no next state means halting. A head move is coded by a natural number: $0$ moves left, $1$ stays,…

results.title: Coded actions as tuples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bijection between coded actions and tuples $(m, w, b, q)$ that sends an action to its coded input head move $m \in \mathbb{N}$, its work tape instructions $w$ (for each of the $k$ work tapes, an optional symbol to write and a coded head move), its optional output bit $b$ and its optional next state $q$.

results.title: Decoding a coded action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A coded action $a$ stands for the action of CSLib's multi-tape model that moves the input head by the decoded input move of $a$, on each work tape writes the optional symbol that $a$ gives for that tape and moves its head by the decoded move, emits the optional output bit of $a$, and enters the next state of $a$ (halting when there is none).

results.title: Halting action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The default action of a missing table entry: halt without moving any head, writing any symbol or emitting an output bit.

results.title: Keys of a code's table
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A key of a table entry for a machine with $k$ work tapes is a triple $(q, a, w)$ of a state $q \in \mathbb{N}$, the symbol $a$ under the input head and the symbols $w = (w_i)_{i < k}$ under the $k$ work heads, where each symbol is a bit or the blank.

results.title: Codes for multi-tape machines
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A code for a machine with $k$ work tapes over the binary alphabet, with states in $\mathbb{N}$, is a finite list of table entries, each a key (a state together with the symbols under the input head and the $k$ work heads) paired with a coded action. The table is looked up by key, the first matching entry wins, and a missing key halts the machine.

results.title: Multi-tape codes as tables
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bijection between codes for machines with $k$ work tapes and finite lists of table entries, each a pair of a key and a coded action, that sends a code to its table.

results.title: Numeric coding of codes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The natural number coding a code $c$: its encoding under the standard primitive recursive coding of codes, which identifies a code with its table, a list of pairs of a key and a coded action.

results.title: Decoding numbers to codes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The code coded by a natural number $n$, if any: decoding under the standard primitive recursive coding of codes, which identifies a code with its table, a list of pairs of a key and a coded action. The result is empty when $n$ codes no code.

results.title: Code round-trip
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every code $c$ with $k$ work tapes, decoding the natural number $\operatorname{encode}(c)$ returns $c$: $\operatorname{decode}(\operatorname{encode}(c))$ is defined and equals $c$.

results.title: Injectivity of the numeric coding of codes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two codes $c$ and $c'$ with the same number of work tapes have the same numeric code, then $c = c'$.

results.title: Action of a code at a key
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes, a state $q \in \mathbb{N}$, a symbol $a$ under the input head and symbols $w = (w_i)_{i < k}$ under the work heads (each symbol a bit or the blank), the action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$ is the coded action of the first table entry of $c$ whose key is $(q, a, w)$, or, if there is no such entry, the halting action, which moves no head, writes and emits nothing, and has no next state.

results.title: Transition function of a code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The transition function of a code $c$ sends a state $q$, the symbol $a$ under the input head and the symbols $w$ under the work heads (each a bit or blank) to the action of CSLib's multi-tape model that the coded action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$ stands for. That coded action is the one of the first table entry of $c$ with key $(q, a, w)$, or, if there is none, the one that halts without moving, writing or emitting.

results.title: The multi-tape machine of a code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The machine of a code $c$ for $k$ work tapes is the machine of CSLib's multi-tape model with $k$ work tapes, the binary alphabet and states in $\mathbb{N}$ whose initial state is $0$ and whose transition function is the transition function of $c$.

results.title: Step of the machine of a code
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$, a binary input $x$ and a configuration $C$ of the machine of $c$ on $x$, the step of the machine of $c$ sends $C$ to its successor under the transition function of $c$: $C$ itself if it has halted, and otherwise the result of applying to $C$ the action that the transition function of $c$ selects for the state of $C$ and the symbols under its heads.

results.title: States of a multi-tape code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The states of a code $c$ for machines with $k$ work tapes form the finite set of natural numbers consisting of the initial state $0$ and the next state of every table entry of $c$ that does not halt.

results.title: Next states of a code lie in its state set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$, a state $q$, an input symbol $a$ and work tape symbols $w$, if the action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$ has a next state $q'$ (rather than halting), then $q'$ belongs to the set of states of $c$.

results.title: Codes denote finite-state machines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a code for a machine with $k$ work tapes. For every binary input $x$ and every number of steps $t$, if the machine of $c$, run for $t$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, has not halted and is in state $q$, then $q$ lies in the finite set of states of $c$.

results.title: Work tapes as zippers
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A work tape is a pair of finite lists of cells, each cell a bit or blank: the cells left of the head, nearest first, and the cells from the head rightwards; cells beyond both lists are blank.

results.title: Symbol under the head of a zipper tape
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The symbol read from a work tape given as a zipper $(l, r)$ is the first cell of $r$, or the blank if $r$ is empty.

results.title: Writing on a zipper tape
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Writing an optional symbol on a work tape leaves the tape unchanged when no symbol is given; given a symbol $s$ (a bit or blank), it replaces the cell under the head by $s$ and keeps all other cells.

results.title: Moving the head of a zipper tape
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a coded move $m$ and a work tape given as a zipper $(l, r)$: if $m = 0$ the head moves one cell left, removing the first cell of $l$ (the blank if $l$ is empty) and putting it in front of $r$; if $m = 1$ the tape is unchanged; otherwise the head moves one cell right, removing the first cell of $r$ (the blank if $r$ is empty) and putting it in front of $l$.

results.title: Cell of a zipper tape
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a work tape $t$ in zipper form and an integer $j$, the cell of $t$ at $j$ is the symbol at offset $j$ from the head: for $j = n \ge 0$ it is entry $n$ (counting from $0$) of the list of cells from the head rightwards, and for $j = -(n + 1)$ it is entry $n$ of the list of cells left of the head, nearest first; in either case it is the blank when the list has no entry $n$.

results.title: Explicit configurations of the code evaluator
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An explicit configuration for a machine with $k$ work tapes consists of an optional state in $\mathbb{N}$ (none when the machine has halted); the input head position, a natural number shifted by one, so that position $0$ is the cell left of the input; the $k$ work tapes, each a zipper (the cells left of the head, nearest first, and the cells from the head rightwards, all further cells blank); and the output written…

results.title: Explicit configurations as tuples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bijection between explicit configurations and tuples $(q, p, t, o)$ that sends a configuration to its optional state $q$ (empty when halted), its shifted input head position $p \in \mathbb{N}$, its family $t$ of $k$ work tapes (each a zipper) and its output $o$ so far, a list of bits.

results.title: Initial configuration of the clocked evaluator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The initial explicit configuration has state $0$, the input head on the first input cell (position $1$, positions being shifted by one), every work tape blank (both halves of its zipper empty), and empty output.

results.title: Input symbol under the input head
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an input $x$ and a shifted input head position $p$, the input symbol is the blank if $p = 0$; otherwise it is the entry of $x$ at index $p - 1$ (counting from $0$) if $p - 1 < |x|$, and the blank if $p - 1 \ge |x|$.

results.title: Input head move of the clocked evaluator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an input of length $n$, a shifted input head position $p$ and a coded move $m$, the new position is $p - 1$ (truncated at $0$) if $m = 0$, $p$ if $m = 1$, and $\min(p + 1, n + 1)$ otherwise, so a move right never passes position $n + 1$, one cell beyond the input.

results.title: Applying a coded action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an input word $x$, a coded action $a$ and an explicit configuration $e$, applying $a$ to $e$ gives the configuration whose state is the next state of $a$; whose input head position is that of $e$, say $p$, moved by the coded input move of $a$, where a left move gives $p - 1$ (truncated at $0$), staying gives $p$, and a right move gives $\min(p + 1, |x| + 1)$; whose work tape $i$ is work tape $i$ of $e$ after…

results.title: Evaluator step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One step of the evaluator for a code $c$ on a binary input $x$ leaves an explicit configuration $e$ unchanged if $e$ has halted; if $e$ is in state $q$, it applies to $e$ the coded action of $c$ at $q$, the input symbol at the input head position of $e$ and the symbols under the heads of the work tapes of $e$.

results.title: Clocked evaluator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The clocked evaluator runs a code $c$ on a binary input $x$ for $T$ steps: it applies the evaluator's step $T$ times to the initial explicit configuration. If the resulting configuration is halted, it returns that configuration's output; otherwise it returns no result.

results.title: Explicit configurations representing machine configurations
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An explicit configuration $e$ represents a configuration $C$ of CSLib's multi-tape model on input $x$ when they have the same state, the same shifted input head position and the same output, and for every work tape $i$ and every cell $z \in \mathbb{Z}$, the content of cell $z$ of tape $i$ in $C$ equals the cell of tape $i$ of $e$ at offset $z - p_i$ from its head, where $p_i$ is the head position of tape $i$ in $C$.

results.title: The evaluator simulates the machine step for step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a code and $x$ a binary input. If an explicit configuration $e$ represents a configuration $C$ of the machine of $c$ on $x$, then the evaluator's step of $e$ for $c$ on $x$ represents the successor of $C$ under the machine of $c$.

results.title: The evaluator tracks the machine run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$, an input $x$ and every $t$, the explicit configuration obtained from the initial one by $t$ steps of the evaluator for $c$ on $x$ represents the configuration that the machine of $c$ reaches after $t$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$.

results.title: Evaluator agreement
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every code $c$, binary input $x$, clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$ and binary word $o$, the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns $o$ if and only if the machine of $c$, run for $T$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, has halted and its output is $o$.

results.title: The evaluator returns within the clock exactly when the machine runs in time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$, an input $x$ and a clock $T$, the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns an output if and only if the machine of $c$ runs in time $T$ on $x$, that is, every computation path of that machine on $x$ with at least $T$ steps ends in a halted configuration.

results.title: Monotonicity of the clocked evaluator for multi-tape codes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$ for machines with $k$ work tapes, a binary input $x$, a binary word $o$ and clocks $T \le T'$ in $\mathbb{N}$, if the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ returns $o$ with clock $T$, then it also returns $o$ with clock $T'$.

results.title: A code computes exactly what its clocked evaluator returns
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes and binary words $x$ and $o$, the machine of $c$ computes $o$ on input $x$, that is, it eventually halts on $x$ with output $o$, if and only if there is a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the clocked evaluator of $c$ run on $x$ for $T$ steps returns $o$.

results.title: The evaluator is primitive recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The evaluator is primitive recursive in the code, the input and the clock.

results.title: Coding head moves
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A head move is coded as a natural number: left is $0$, stay is $1$ and right is $2$. Decoding a move code recovers the move.

The coded action of an action $a$ of the machine under $e$ records as its input-head move the code of the input-head move of $a$ (left $0$, stay $1$, right $2$); for each work tape it records what $a$ writes there and the code of the head move of $a$ there; it records the output bit of $a$, if any; and its next…

results.title: Decoding the coding of an action
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $Q$ be a type, $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$ a map and $a$ an action of a binary machine with $k$ work tapes and states in $Q$. The action that the coded action of $a$, with its successor state numbered by $e$, stands for is $a$ with its successor state relabelled by $e$.

results.title: State bound of a code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The states of a code $c$ are the initial state $0$ and every successor state named in its table. The state bound of $c$ is one more than the largest of them; it is a strict upper bound on the states of $c$.

results.title: A number as a bounded state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $N$ and $q$, this is $q$ as an element of $\{0, \dots, N - 1\}$ if $q < N$, and no value otherwise.

results.title: Transition function of a code on bounded states
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $c$ be a code with $k$ work tapes and let $N$ be its state bound. For a state $q < N$, a symbol $a$ under the input head and symbols $w$ under the $k$ work heads (each a bit or blank), this is the action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$ with the same input-head move, work-tape writes and moves, and output, and with its successor state read as a state below $N$; a successor state that is not below $N$ is replaced by halting.

results.title: A code's machine simulates its finite-state machine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every code $c$, the machine of $c$ simulates the finite-state machine of $c$ up to the relabelling that sends each state $q < N$, where $N$ is the state bound of $c$, to the natural number $q$.

results.title: The code of a machine simulates it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a machine over the binary alphabet with $k$ work tapes, a finite set of states $Q$ and initial state $q_0$, and let $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$ be injective with $e(q_0) = 0$. Then the machine of the code of $M$ with states numbered by $e$ simulates $M$ up to the relabelling $e$.

results.title: Numbering a finite type from a chosen element
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite type $Q$ and every $q_0 \in Q$ there is an injective map $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$ with $e(q_0) = 0$.

results.title: Every finite-state machine has a code
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A binary machine with finitely many states is simulated, up to an injective state relabelling, by the machine of some code.

results.title: DTIME over codes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every language $L$ of binary words, $L \in \mathsf{DTIME}(t)$ if and only if there are natural numbers $c_1, c_2, k$ and a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes such that the machine of $c$ decides $L$, on every input $w$ runs in time $c_1 t(|w|) + c_2$, and for some $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ on every input $w$ runs in space $s(|w|)$.

results.title: DSPACE over codes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every language $L$ of binary words, $L \in \mathsf{DSPACE}(s)$ if and only if there are natural numbers $c_1, c_2, k$ and a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes such that the machine of $c$ decides $L$, on every input $w$ runs in space $c_1 s(|w|) + c_2$, and for some $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ on every input $w$ runs in time $t(|w|)$.
